The Interactions API is now generally available. 🎉 The Interactions API is the simplest way to build with Gemini for humans and agents. 

- One API for Gemini models and agents.
- Antigravity Agent with a isolated remote Linux sandbox.
- Image gen with Nano Banana; music with Lyria 3, soon video with Omni.
- `background=True` for async, long-running interactions.
- Multimodal Tool Use & Combination.
- Dedicated skills for coding agent.

Building something new inside Google isn't easy, but it's possible. We spent almost a year on this because we think developers and agents deserve an API that is intuitive, familiar and easy to learn and use and evolves with improving capabilities and new behaviors. 

Give it a try. Feature requests, bugs, complaints all to me. 👇🏻

We just shipped Dynamic Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API.

- Defer functions and remote MCP servers
- Server-side tool search.
- Client-side mode works, e.g. Gemini Decision 1

Stop loading 200 tool on turn 1.

Genie 4 is the first model we launched on the new Live Interactions API, bringing native WebRTC (with ephemeral tokens) and WebSocket support directly to Interactions and Gemini API.

This is part of our ongoing work to improve Gemini API experience. When we started building the Interactions API, one of our main goals was making sure standard API calls and real-time and long running sessions share one consistent interface. We put a lot of effort into getting the primitives right, and we have big plans.

I would love your feedback as we build this out: what do you want to see as we bring protocols like WebSockets and WebRTC to more Gemini models? What is still missing for building better agent experiences or real-time apps?

My Gemini 4 model guidance:

Neon = Daily driver for coding and agents ($3/$15). I mostly use Neon now. 

Hydrogen = fastest, cheapest ($1.50/$7.50). Use for basic tasks/chat or subagents. 

Carbon = Opened tasks that are ok to be slower. Testing, Simulations for complex long-horizon runs
Neon is great model browser use

Agent harnesses should replace built-in multi-agent features with an MCP servers of the harness itself.

Use the same loop/cli recursively to create new threads ... or search in them. Use MCP events for subscriptions. You could rebuild message board collaboration for model 1 and have orechstrator pattern for model 2

Much easier to iterate or upgrade.
Great example for the Google Decision 1 audio capability.

Evaluations are the backbone of any frontier progress. Today we're launching MKA (Multimodal Knowledge Agent) with @ArtificialAnlys, a benchmark for agents doing knowledge work on visually complex files.

- 200 tasks across 10 verticals and 83 occupations, written by domain experts
- Each task takes a seasoned professional 3 to 8 hours
- ~70 yes/no rubric checks per task, weighted 75% factual accuracy and 25% visual design
- Every model runs in the same harness (Stirrup) with the same tools, sandbox and turn budget
- 200 tasks stay private with Artificial Analysis, so they can't leak into training data
- 10 public tasks on @huggingface 🤗

Gemini 4 Carbon is #2 on quality, 3 points behind Claude Fable 5.2, at $6.29 per task vs $31.97.
